headline: Highest risk is medium: gpt-researcher can ingest files and browse while plano has broad egress, creating plausible leakage and unverified-output cascades; no direct shared-channel evidence raises confidence limits.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read local files and run browsers, and plano accepts OpenAI-compatible inputs with broad egress. If plano outputs attacker-controlled text that gpt-researcher later ingests via files or copied research artifacts, instruction hijacking is plausible. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF plano output is fed into gpt-researcher as a file or prompt without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or MCP bridge, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of plano outputs into gpt-researcher.
Add a prompt-sanitization step before any cross-agent handoff.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Require human review for any text copied between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress; plano also has broad egress and handles logs/metrics. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive local documents to outbound APIs. No direct evidence of a shared filesystem exists, so this is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local documents or workspace, leakage risk is present.
IF either agent forwards copied content to external APIs, sensitive material can leave the host.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory.
Block outbound access for any agent handling sensitive files.
Redact documents before passing them to either agent.
Review API destinations configured in both agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can install packages, read files, spawn subprocesses, and browse; plano cannot spawn subprocesses and is out-of-process dataplane oriented. Their write surfaces are not documented as overlapping, so direct resource conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because shared mutable resources are not fully specified.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable project directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same git or config state, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared config files.
Serialize package installation steps.
Use a lock file for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, while plano is a gateway/proxy style agent that can route or relay outputs. If plano treats gpt-researcher’s report as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or routing decisions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF plano consumes gpt-researcher reports without independent verification, cascading errors are possible.
IF gpt-researcher outputs are used as facts for downstream automation, mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require source verification before plano acts on any report.
Add a confidence threshold for downstream use.
Keep a human approval step for high-impact outputs.
Log provenance for every cross-agent handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. gpt-researcher handles secrets and local documents, while plano handles logs and metrics, but no regulated-data pathway is documented. Because the compliance surface is underspecified, I do not escalate beyond low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through gpt-researcher into plano logs, compliance risk increases.
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not present in either profile, a mismatch exists.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair.
Review logging settings in both agents.
Separate secret-bearing workflows from analytics/logging workflows.
Document retention and deletion handling before deployment.
